{"title":"Live issue-sweep run parked itself: driver interrupt-released, reclaim released all children","body":"## Problem

The live issue-sweep run `run-1` (runner checkout `~/smithers-runner` at `007c0d94`, owner pid 29504, 33 work children in local microVMs) parked itself at 2026-10-01T05:13:36Z. No operator issued a control command. The host process kept running, but every child was released, every microVM was removed, and Burndown's cleanup released all 33 in-flight claims as `failed: round died`. Those rows are settled, so resuming the run cannot retry them.

Journal (`smthrs runs logs run-1 --after 6080`):

```
6085 05:13:20 run-decision run-1 interrupt-released  (status suspended, waiting.reason "released", cancelRequestedAtMs null)
6086 05:13:21 flows.agent.budget-suspended.v1 run-1
6087 05:13:21 run-decision registry/entry/... interrupt-released
6089 05:13:23 run-decision run-1 claimed-and-activated
6090 05:13:23 run-decision run-1 resumed
6091-6126 05:13:30-36 run-decision issue-sweep/<n>/attempt-8 interrupt-released  (x33)
6127 05:13:36 control.run.parked  parkedBy = the run's own owner {pid 29504}
```

`RunDriver.ts` writes `interrupt-released` only when the driver fiber is interrupted without a recorded cancel request (issue #26 path). Something in the host interrupted run-1's driver fiber. The host then reclaimed and resumed the run, and on the second pass released all of its children and parked it. The host log (`.flows/logs/run-1.log`) holds only the admission line, so no cause was recorded.

At the time the machine had load average ~100 on 16 cores, 7 GiB of swap in use, and a 12 GiB image-builder microVM running.

## Expected

- A run that no one asked to stop keeps running. If the host must release it, the journal records why (lease loss, defect, signal).
- A reclaim after a release re-drives the children it reattaches to. It does not release them and park.
- A park must not settle in-flight Burndown items as `failed: round died` when the run is expected to resume.

- a real-VM restart test keeps an outside sentinel unchanged after the guest plants links at script and heartbeat paths.

Until then, Smithers passes no `scripts` to agent machines.

{"title":"Diagnose runtime OPFS write failure after Wiki retries","body":"## Observed

On the signed-in Canary app, a Wiki refresh returned a handled HTTP 409 because the repository's history did not exist. After two Wiki attempts on one page, the app later switched to the fatal **Changes could not be saved** panel. Reload restored the prior cards and conversation. A subsequent single Wiki 409 left the app responsive for more than two minutes. Browser storage reported about 3.1 MB used against a much larger quota, and there was no storage error in the console.

The 409 is temporal context, **not an established cause**. The page was also open in another inactive tab; no writer takeover was requested during this reproduction.

## Source boundary

`AppStore.persistStream` reports `StorageWriteFailedError` for any OPFS persistence rejection and discards the original exception from host diagnostics. The fail-closed UI is intentional, but current evidence cannot distinguish an actual SQLite/OPFS I/O failure from a quota fault, stale writer, or storage conflict. `StackSeam.refreshWiki` handles a 409 as a request failure; one 409 does not reproduce the fatal panel.

## Acceptance

- Preserve the fail-closed writer behavior and committed rows. Never replay an uncertain act on reload.
- Reproduce rapid Wiki retries against the real SQLite adapter and test their durable write/notice behavior.
- Emit a bounded, content-free failure classification for an OPFS write rejection (no raw exception text, SQL, row keys, paths, credentials, or user data), with regression coverage for known fault classes and unknown errors.
- Use a fresh served-build reproduction to identify the actual failing class and fix the cause under this issue or a linked follow-up; do not close from instrumentation alone.

{"title":"Flows have no sanctioned way to use operator credentials from a confined child","body":"## Problem

A confined flow child cannot use the operator's own credentials, and there is no sanctioned way to grant them.

Since capability enforcement reached action bodies (eaf9a7e9), every spawn runs under seatbelt with a private `HOME`, reads limited to `fs:read` grants, and writes limited to the workspace root. Operator bookkeeping needs the operator's state:

| Tool | State it needs |
| --- | --- |
| `gh`, `scripts/issue-claim.mjs` | `~/.config/gh`, `~/.config/issue-claim`, `~/.cache/issue-claim` throttle |
| `codex-rr`, `claude-rr` | `~/.smithers/accounts/*` (logins, rotation state) |
| `jj git push` | SSH keys / git credentials |
| `jj workspace add` outside the checkout | writes beside the workspace root |

`flows/issue-sweep` works around this by running those commands through an unconfined host spawner (`NodeServices.layer`, `flows/issue-sweep/host.ts`). That bypasses the capability ceiling entirely: the flow's declared `proc:spawn:*` capabilities document intent but enforce nothing for those calls.

## Expected

A declared, approvable grant for operator credentials, e.g. a capability such as `cred:gh` or `fs:read:~/.config/gh/**` that keeps `HOME` but still confines everything else, so a flow never needs an unconfined escape hatch.

## Evidence

- `flows/issue-sweep/host.ts` (header comment) and `flows/issue-sweep/work/flow.ts` cloud path.
- docs/blog/building-burndown-notes.md, "Smithers bugs found" item 3.

{"title":"Packaged app: Electrobun frees a cold-launch smithers:// link before the app reads it","body":"A cold launch by `smithers://open/<owner>/<repo>` almost never reaches the window: Electrobun 2.0.1 frees the buffered link before its threadsafe callback reads it.

## Evidence (found while proving #1969)

Stable bundle built from main, cold-launched 10 times through LaunchServices with an isolated HOME and the E2E bridge:

```
open -n -a apps/app/build/stable-macos-arm64/Smithers.app --env HOME=<tmp> --env SMITHERS_E2E_BRIDGE=1 ... smithers://open/smithersai/smithers
```

| result | runs |
| --- | --- |
| first window at `/smithersai/smithers` | 0 / 10 |
| link delivered as garbage, refused by `deepLinkPath` | 8 / 10 |
| link arrived after the window (loadURL) | 1 / 10 |
| no link observed | 1 / 10 |

With the refusal log instrumented to print the received string, the `open-url` payloads were `"\^D"`, `"com.apple.spotlight.IndexAgent.workloop"`, `""` and random bytes: freed memory.

## Cause

`nativeWrapper.mm` (Electrobun 2.0.1 and current `blackboardsh/electrobun` main):

```objc
extern "C" void setURLOpenHandler(URLOpenHandler handler) {
    std::vector<std::string> pending;
    { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_urlOpenMutex); g_urlOpenHandler = handler; pending = std::move(g_pendingUrlOpenPaths); }
    for (const auto& url : pending) handler(url.c_str());   // handler is a threadsafe JSCallback: it only queues the pointer
}                                                           // `pending` is destroyed here; the queued pointer now dangles
```

The SDK registers the handler as `new JSCallback(..., { args: [FFIType.cstring], threadsafe: true })`, which Bun runs later as a task, after the strings are freed. `smthrs workspace create --cpus 4 --memory 8192 --disk 32768 --idle-timeout 1800` advertises and sends resource options via packages/smithers/src/internal/backend/Workspaces.ts:workspaceBody. It also exposes image/network/allow/service options. The public createWorkspaceRequest in packages/backend/internal/routes/workspace.go:139–145 accepts only name, snapshot_id, source_bookmark, kind, environment, and its decoder at line 366 does not reject unknown fields. CreateWorkspaceInput has no corresponding requested resources. Thus these options are silently discarded, and the CLI has no kind option to select the supported VM environment.

Observed Cloud creation returned a running container; execution succeeded, but df showed a 2 GiB root disk despite a 32 GiB request. The workspace reported .smithers/environment.nix with empty revision/closure and had Node/Bun/pnpm/jj, without Go/PostgreSQL. Running does not mean the requested execution environment was applied. Private operational receipts stay in smithersai/plue#507.

Acceptance:
- Make the CLI and public create API one explicit contract: honor supported settings through persistence, admission, create/recovery/fork, and exact allocation reporting, or refuse unsupported settings before provisioning. No silently ignored options.
- Expose the existing kind/environment selection coherently, including the repository Nix VM path; do not add a second provider-specific creation path.
- Behavioral CLI-to-real-HTTP boundary tests catch option loss; backend tests prove durable requested/effective resource agreement and bounded admission. Assert unknown/unsupported fields and invalid combinations refuse.
- Live receipt verifies effective CPU/RAM/disk and requested toolchain on the created guest.
